stem.en: Two sources make sound in the same room. Source A vibrates 200 times each second. Source B vibrates 400 times each second. Both waves travel through the same air. How do the two waves compare?

text.en: B's wave has more energy, because B vibrates faster.
The two waves are the same in every way, because they travel through the same air.
B's wave has twice the frequency and half the wavelength of A's wave, and both travel at the same speed.
B's wave travels faster, because B vibrates faster.

explanation.en: B's wave has a frequency of 400 Hz and A's has 200 Hz. In the same air, both travel at the same speed. Since v = λ × ν, doubling the frequency halves the wavelength.

hints.en: Use v = λ × ν. Which of the three stays the same in the same air?
If the speed stays the same and the frequency doubles, what happens to the wavelength?
